runtimeAcceptance: NP01-NP10 NOT_RUN; documentary adequacy is not runtime PASS

findings.title: The input and executable identity chain is not defined completely
findings.observation: The report names driverSha256/profileSha256 without defining their byte domains or bundle recipe. Binary handles/pre-post checks cover the selected toolchain, but no equivalent rule covers the trusted observer, client wrapper and imported helpers. The closed report has no manifest digest or mandatory artifact mapping for the exact consumed manifest, stdin and resolved profile. A generic artifacts list could carry these, but the SPEC does not require that inventory.
findings.counterexample: Change an observer/helper while retaining the CLI script, toolchain and semantic manifest values. Both implementations can choose the same driverSha256/profileSha256 under the current undefined recipe; the reviewer cannot determine which trusted collector was executed. This is an underspecified contract, not a demonstrated exploit.
findings.impact: NP08 requires alteration of any input to invalidate its binding. Pinning only the three binaries cannot establish that property for the observation software and input.
findings.required_correction: Define raw/canonical digest domains and the deterministic bundle/profile recipe, including the controller, both wrappers/collector, imported helpers, synthetic settings/MCP, literal stdin, fixed argv/env template and resolved run-specific values. Require a retained consumed-input inventory and bind it to Reportv1, either through defined artifacts or explicit fields. State which snapshots/handles are used, when drift is checked and which status it causes. This needs no distributed signature or new trust service.
findings.closure: Documentary examples must let a reviewer recompute the same digests from retained bytes. Future negatives must change a helper, observer, manifest bytes, fixture/config and resolved invocation independently and defeat the relevant integrity check before launch or invalidate the run afterward. No digest used to grant PORT_OBSERVED may be null.

findings.title: The trusted observation protocol does not yet specify the native POST to fixed 503 proof
findings.observation: The collector/client separation is sound in direction, but the only specified host command is START_NATIVE. READY/preflight, version/port phase boundaries, child execution results and observer events have no closed framing or ordering contract. Version and prompt invocations are both allowed after START_NATIVE. Clock origin/offset derivation across containers is unspecified. The fixed 503 response has no frozen body/header bytes or required response completion record; observations describe requests only.
findings.counterexample: An eligible callback followed by a response write/connection failure is not by itself evidence of the required POST503 exchange. Similarly, a request during the version phase is after START_NATIVE but is not evidence of the prompt probe. These paths need a rejectable event contract, not assumptions about current Claude behavior.
findings.impact: NP03 rejects fake stdout, NP04 requires real launch/lineage and NP05 requires a real POST503. The current text does not define enough evidence to check those claims independently.
findings.required_correction: Freeze a small bounded host/wrapper/observer event protocol with source ownership, phases, framing, required fields, duplicate/out-of-order/EOF rejection and one time reference or explicit host ordering. Specify how native bytes remain data and how actual child exit/signal is obtained. Only the prompt-probe phase may contribute eligible observations. Freeze the synthetic 503 bytes/headers and require protected collector evidence of response outcome tied to the request; distinguish local response completion from proof that the client consumed it. State the local trust assumption: host, wrappers and collector are trusted reviewed software; the public synthetic sentinel is a routing/fixture guard, not authentication of a particular process.
findings.closure: Future negatives must cover client stdout containing fake events, malformed/duplicate control frames, POST before the prompt phase, missing native-start/result evidence and response failure after request receipt. None may manufacture the claimed exchange. A retained positive trace must identify the pinned prompt invocation and its actual observer-generated 503 outcome. No model response or functional adapter is requested.

findings.title: Uncertain Docker creation and failed cleanup lack a bounded recovery contract
findings.observation: The SPEC permits management only of created IDs checked against labels, gives deterministic names and requires cleanup within 5s. It does not say how ownership is recovered if Docker creates a container but its ID reply is lost, or how a controller crash/daemon outage is represented and handed off. NP07 states no container/process remains, which cannot be guaranteed within the deadline when the daemon cannot answer. Native output/artifact limits also do not explicitly allocate bounds for control/observer/Docker streams or daemon logging.
findings.counterexample: docker create succeeds at the daemon, then the CLI times out before returning the ID. Retrying create may duplicate an uncertain effect; ID-only cleanup cannot address the container without a defined exact-identity reconciliation. A daemon outage can also outlast the cleanup budget.
findings.impact: This is an NP07 failure-path feasibility gap, and a resource/evidence boundary for NP06/NP08. A time-bounded failure is possible; a time-bounded unconditional no-orphan guarantee is not.
findings.required_correction: Record role/name/run nonce and creation intent before each create. Specify an exact-name/identity recovery procedure with full labels and image/config verification, no adoption of unrelated containers, no global inventory and no repeated uncertain create. Define crash/cancellation ownership and a finite unresolved-cleanup handoff containing only owned identities. Unconfirmed cleanup must yield INFRA_FAILURE/incomplete evidence and cannot satisfy NP07 or publish PORT_OBSERVED. Scope the 20s/30s/5s clocks to all relevant operations and bound subprocess/control buffers and daemon logging without expanding resources.
findings.closure: Future injected cases must cover create-completed/reply-lost, second create failure, inspect timeout, daemon unavailable during cleanup, controller cancellation/crash and primary-plus-cleanup failure. Each must produce either verified removal or an explicit owned unresolved-resource record, preserve all causes and avoid false clean/PORT_OBSERVED. Document the bounded human/Lead recovery next action when removal cannot be confirmed.

findings.title: Reportv1 is closed by name but is missing the evidence invariants needed for rejection
findings.observation: containmentChecks has no required ID set/order/uniqueness or mapping to real inspect/preflight evidence. Artifacts has no required roles or uniqueness/cardinality relationship to observations. Classified content-type/content-encoding and temporal evidence required at lines147-151 have no defined retained record location. A real native SIGABRT/SIGSEGV cannot be faithfully represented by the closed SIGTERM/SIGKILL/null field if that signal was observed.
findings.counterexample: A report containing one arbitrary PASS check and a syntactically valid observation has no explicit schema-level missing-check rule. An artifact digest could point to unrelated bytes unless the observation-to-body/event relationship is mandatory. This does not mean such a report obeys the prose; it means its deterministic rejection contract is incomplete.
findings.impact: The independent reviewer cannot mechanically distinguish complete real controls from a selectively populated report. A closed schema must represent genuine failures as well as the intended path.
findings.required_correction: Define the mandatory control IDs, their source artifacts and state/order rules, plus bounded list/type/uniqueness/path invariants. Require each observation to resolve to the exact raw body and protected event record, including encoding classifications, phase/time relation and response outcome from R1-02. State which absent evidence makes PORT_OBSERVED impossible. Allow faithful recording/classification of other observed native signals; reserve null for genuinely unobserved information with a limitation. Keep this report REFERENCE_RECON_ONLY.
findings.closure: Future report validation must reject missing/duplicate required checks, PASS without required raw evidence, digest/size mismatch, duplicated/out-of-range ordinals and wrong phase/body links. A synthetic non-TERM/KILL native signal must have a valid honest failure representation. This is a documentary schema correction, not a request to add product capabilities.

findings.title: Failure precedence leaves privacy violations and concurrent failures ambiguous
findings.observation: The status paragraph lists categories but does not fully define competing runtime failures. A non-synthetic auth/token/cookie is a recorded violation, yet its terminal classification and effect on a previously eligible POST are absent. A toolchain digest failure overlaps hash INVALID_INPUT and toolchain INFRA_FAILURE; blocked preflight plus cleanup failure also has no explicit precedence. A required check failing must not be overridden by an earlier eligible POST.
findings.counterexample: Observe one eligible POST, then reject a request carrying forbidden auth, then encounter cleanup failure. The report must preserve all causes and deterministically select a non-success status; choosing between the available categories is currently left to the builder.
findings.impact: The scope promises fail-closed privacy and integrity, and exit0 only for an intact observation. That is testable only with a frozen terminal decision rule.
findings.required_correction: Provide an ordered phase/failure table covering invalid CLI/input, missing/mismatched/incompatible toolchain, preflight failure, forbidden auth, request/output cap, native timeout/exit, control protocol failure, late drift, IO and cleanup failure. Freeze the terminal status, exit code, retained primary/additional causes and later NOT_RUN checks. Explicitly deny PORT_OBSERVED whenever a required safety/integrity check fails, even after an eligible request. Define marker/opaque-body outcomes consistently with the intentionally port-only goal; do not add a functional-parity requirement.
findings.closure: Documentary cases must have exactly one expected status/exit/check chain for eligible-POST plus forbidden auth, cap overflow, timeout, digest drift, cleanup failure and final publication failure, as well as preflight plus cleanup dual failure. Future tests must preserve that mapping and never silently downgrade a violation to PORT_NOT_OBSERVED or success.

optional.title: Reuse the qualified publication mechanism explicitly
optional.detail: Existing Q01 safe-io.mjs:336-398 and qualify.mjs:523-618 already show staging, close-before-publish and final exclusive report.json publication. Their static source is feasible support for the intended rule. An explicit normative reference and frozen helper identity would save reimplementation. Preserve its pending/final distinction and apply the probe-specific 8MiB cap; this is a reuse suggestion, not a requirement to import the qualifier or rewrite publication.

optional.title: Explain marker/protocol limits near the successful port result
optional.detail: The marker and recognized JSON are intentionally separate from eligible transport observation. A short example of PORT_OBSERVED with an opaque body would help operators avoid treating it as SDK/model qualification. Do not strengthen the probe into semantic or functional parity.

criteria.reason: Closed input shape/caps are useful; complete identity and failure mapping are missing.
none/container network plus real inspect/preflight is a credible design; complete required evidence and uncertain-create ownership need definition.
Separate collector PID/filesystem/stdout defeats the stated fake-stdout route; event origin and report bindings still need a contract.
Fixed env/argv and delayed native launch are appropriate; phase/lineage evidence and trusted bundle identity remain underspecified.
A native POST followed by a deliberate fixed error is a valid narrow goal; actual response/probe-phase evidence and failure outcomes need closure.
Request/body/native byte caps and auth discard are good controls; all channels and privacy failures must have bounded deterministic handling.
Cleanup uncertainty must remain explicit; daemon failure cannot be equated to verified removal.
Exclusive evidence/publication direction is sound; reproducible input/raw/event binding and terminal failure handling need definition.
REFERENCE_RECON_ONLY, no compatible functional receipt, no catalogue credit/model/account and no 0229-derived authority are explicit.

criteria.documentaryAssessment: Documentarily adequate subject to corrected freeze
criteria.reason: Exact human T3 review, same-candidate qualified dependencies/gates and independent code review before native launch are required. All execution evidence remains NOT_RUN.

limitations: Static design adequacy only. No compatibility, native transport, containment or cleanup runtime claim was verified. Source inspection was limited to existing Q01 publication feasibility. Frozen recon is evidence of literal bytes/declarations, not supported transport.
No malicious-host, image-runtime attestation or cryptographic process-authentication claim is made.
Shared ledger changes by concurrent owners are outside this freeze; this critic wrote only its delegated files and private temporary artifacts.
nextAction: Lead corrects only mandatory contract gaps, freezes a new SPEC/packet and returns the changed contract for bounded corrective review. Then obtain explicit human T3 approval of the accepted exact SPEC; only afterward BUILD/code review and separately claimed native execution/gates.
